# Introduction
This analysis uses data from an Integrating Behavioral Health and Primary Care (IBH-PC) to look at whether depression scores improved more in the intervention than in the control. First, I wanted to understand more about the demographics, including distribution of baseline depression by sex and age distribution of participants, and then I visualized the presence of depression in the treatment and control arms at baseline and the two follow-up periods during the study.


# Descriptive Analysis

## Tabular Analysis
```{r, table1}
table_one <- readRDS(
  file = here::here("outputs/table_one.rds")
)
table_one
```

This table displays the distribution of baseline depression by sex. Here we see that over half of female participants reported depression, while under half of male participants reported depression at baseline. 


# Graphical Analysis

## Histogram: Age Distribution
```{r, plot1-data}
knitr::include_graphics(
  here::here("outputs/histogram.png")
)
```

The figure shows that the age distribution of participants was left skewed, meaning that more older participants were included in the study.

## Bar Chart: Depression Distribution

```{r, plot2-data}
knitr::include_graphics(
  here::here("outputs/stacked_bar.png")
)

```

This figure compares the proportion of people in the treatment (active) and control arms reporting depression at the three data collection points in the study. Based on this visual, there does not appear to be a significant difference in the rates of depression seen in the treatment and control arms throughout the study.
